Apple ConnectEd Grant 2014; iPads issued K-12; since 2019 all 9-12 students also receive MacBook Air annually
Chromebooks confirmed as student devices; B Tech E events 2019; Bond Measure L 2014 funded tech; COVID-era distribution 2020; exact 1:1 launch year not documented in public sources
Leasing program started 2019-20 SY at North Oldham MS only; not district-wide; other schools use BYOD or shared carts

EmpowerED for Learning Initiative; 2016-17 SY first year; piloted spring 2016; students in 6th grade issued Chromebook, keep through 8th then district transfers ownership; fee waiver program for low-income
$199M bond referendum passed March 2016; Chromebooks provided to every Grades 3-8 student; facility improvements and new schools also funded; HS had separate 1-to-1 Learning Initiative
All students provided 1:1 technology K-6; specific launch year not documented; COVID-era distribution confirmed 2020; upper bound only
Emergency Smart School Investment Plan submitted March 2020; July 2020 state approved; 5,000 Chromebooks ordered and distributed; fully funded via Smart Schools funds; goal PreK-12 1:1
1:1 ratio for technology confirmed for all high school students; specific launch year not documented; pre-COVID evidence implied; upper bound 2020
All students have Google Chromebook; students pick up Chromebook daily at school arrival; specific launch year not found; upper bound 2020
8,500 devices distributed week of Apr 6 2020 (COVID); district ensured one device per student; Verizon Innovative Learning at 2 MS also launched fall 2020 with iPads/Chromebooks
Announced June 7 2019; 1:1 initiative for middle and high school students for 2019-20 SY; devices from existing inventory + purchased additional $150 Chromebooks; COVID expanded to K-12
Aug 2013: opened 2 new middle schools; all 7th-8th grade students issued iPad 1:1 with take-home; district-provided resource; Chromebooks added later for other grades
1:1 iPad program documented by Nov 2015 (guidelines dated 11/03/2015); grades 3-12 district issued; K-2 shared classroom sets; $25/yr insurance program; exact launch year not found - upper bound 2015
Take-home device protection plan offered for CGMS students; Chromebook program documented; specific launch year not found; upper bound 2020

No clear evidence of a 1:1 device program; Aug 2020 only selling/lending laptops to students without home computer access; not a district-wide 1:1 rollout; some student reviews mention low Chromebook supply
2016: 1,400 Chromebooks purchased ($417K) for shared carts; 2018-19 BYOCB initiative; 2020: full 1:1 for grades 6-12 with take-home Chromebooks issued in 6th and 9th grade

1:World digital conversion initiative; 2016-17 HS Chromebook handbook published; every rising 9th grader issued Chromebook through HS; full district (K-8 added later); one-to-one district per 2020 sources
1:M initiative; launched 2014-15 SY after research/pilot; one of Kentucky's early 1:1 adopters; researched, tested devices, consulted peers, fiscal review prior to launch
District known for strong technology program; 'many one-to-one schools'; not fully district-wide; each student has laptop or tablet in 1:1 schools; fiber-optic network district-wide; upper bound 2020
COVID-era: each PVSD student assigned Chromebook Aug 2020 for distance learning; pre-COVID some schools had partial 1:1 (not all schools by Mar 2020); full district 1:1 achieved via COVID response
Chromebooks and iPads confirmed district devices; network infrastructure supports all 12 schools; COVID-era distribution documented 2020; specific 1:1 launch year not found; upper bound 2020
Web to One Initiative; launched Nov 26 2018 (Trimester 2) at Monroe MS then Rolling Hills MS; take-home 1:1 for all middle school students; 99%+ participation rate; district-wide expanded later

Pilot 2011: 10 shared Chromebooks per HS classroom; 2012: full 1:1 for 4,300 HS students; 2016: 2,600 MS students received Lenovo Thinkpad Chromebooks; 2018 expanding to elementary 4th-5th; 5-year digital conversion plan begun spring 2014
COVID-era device distribution; Chromebooks issued to virtual academy students 2021; limited evidence of district-wide 1:1; Technology Resources dept supports educational technology; upper bound 2020
